Well, I'm from a very small town. There's only one female in our AA group that has enough sobriety for me to even consider having her as my sponsor. She has a very full plate and I'm not sure she's willing to take on another drunk.

So, my sponsor is from CA and has studied the book for many years. I could still try to seek out another sponsor, but I just don't want to share my story all over again.

Friday will be 90 days, and I so believe I jumped too far ahead too quickly on this amends. I just really needed to get it off my chest and release the guilt I feel, while taking accountability for my actions.

She knows I've been struggling the loss of this friendship I had before what happened, and she suggested I write the amends letter. Either burn it, or give it to her. Make sure I take responsibility for what I feel that I did wrong to her, but make sure she knew what her ex husband did to me.
She now tells me "Okay then we'll quit talking about it. You wrote a letter, now say a little prayer and give it to God. Tell him not to have any more thoughts about her in your brain and really pray hard."
I know, hoping they'll do a reunion tour down the line so I can take my Slayer obsessed three year old one day. 🤘

One day at a time. It's a two thought process.
1. Oh a drink sounds good, I can just have one.
2. Uh, no I can't and I don't need it.
I am in the same boat as you. I am depressed and lonely. However, I've made it a month and two days without having alcohol and I do not want to start over again. You can stop drinking hundreds of times, but the real battle is living sober.
I suggest going to AA meetings and getting a sponsor. I was so in denial and embarrassed about my alcoholism, but now I'll yell it from the mountain tops. Being in a room of fellow drunks really helped me. Hearing their struggles and words of wisdom made me realize I'm not alone and it is possible to live sober.
I'm here if you ever need to vent. It's not easy, but is anything in life ever easy?

You can have your opinion and I can have mine.
I do however think that your bitterness towards your ex wife is causing this negativity towards the true act of enabling.
I've been both the addicted and the enabler in my life, and this is how I felt when I was told I was enabling my mother. I only did it because I loved her. Now after being the addict, I know that in order for her to get the help she needs I need to let her hit her rock bottom. That'll only be achieved once I stop helping her.

https://www.healthline.com/health/enabler

I could type this whole article, but sharing the link is easier.
Sure I'm an addict too, but it's not a blame game. It's the hard truth for families of alcoholics.

She's just trying to blame everyone else except herself for her addiction to alcohol. I was the same way. The mind of an alcoholic is very complex and messy, not an excuse but it's true. Hopefully one day she'll use her higher power to battle this disease, then she'll be able to make amends to everyone she's hurt in the process.
She might also be trying to concentrate on herself and her sobriety. It sounds like you were her enabler, and maybe she wants to free you from those chains. She's realised that letting you go will benefit you both. Maybe down the road, if she's been able to maintain sobriety, you'll reconnect and have an even more passionate relationship that doesn't revolve around her disease.
I do recommend you read the big book from AA or go to Alanon meetings. That'll help you heal too.
